question: Which of the following is NOT correctly matched? [Maratha territory and the European power that had major conflict there]
options: Bassein – British trading post before Maratha control
Panipat – site of the Third Battle of Panipat fought between Marathas and the British
wrong_fact: The Third Battle of Panipat (1761) was fought between the Marathas and Ahmad Shah Abdali (Durrani Empire of Afghanistan), NOT the British.
explanation: The Third Battle of Panipat in 1761 was a decisive defeat of the Marathas by Ahmad Shah Durrani and his Indian allies. Salsette was taken from the Portuguese by the Marathas and then seized by the British in 1775. Bassein (Treaty of Bassein, 1802) became a key point of British-Maratha conflict. Pune was the seat of the Peshwa.

question: Which of the following is NOT correctly matched? [Treaty / Agreement – Place / Region associated with Maratha-European relations]
options: Treaty of Salbai (1782) – signed after the First Anglo-Maratha War
Treaty of Bassein (1802) – Peshwa Baji Rao II sought British protection
Treaty of Purandar (1776) – Marathas ceded Salsette to the British
Treaty of Mangalore (1784) – ended conflict between the Marathas and Hyder Ali of Mysore
wrong_fact: The Treaty of Mangalore (1784) was signed between the British East India Company and Tipu Sultan of Mysore, ending the Second Anglo-Mysore War. It had nothing to do with the Marathas.
explanation: Treaty of Salbai ended the First Anglo-Maratha War restoring the pre-war status quo. Treaty of Bassein (1802) made the Peshwa a British subsidiary, triggering the Second Anglo-Maratha War. Treaty of Purandar (1776) was indeed signed between the Marathas and the British at Purandar fort near Pune, ceding Salsette. Treaty of Mangalore involved Tipu Sultan vs. the British, not Marathas.

question: Which of the following is NOT correctly matched? [Maratha chief / Sardars – their primary territory]
wrong_fact: The Gaekwads were the rulers of Baroda (Vadodara) in Gujarat, NOT Kolhapur. Kolhapur was ruled by a separate branch of the Bhonsle family (descendants of Rajaram).
explanation: The five major Maratha confederacy chiefs: Peshwas controlled Pune; Scindias controlled Gwalior/Ujjain; Holkars controlled Indore; Bhonsles controlled Nagpur; and Gaekwads controlled Baroda (Gujarat). The British concluded subsidiary alliance treaties with each of these chiefs separately, culminating in their defeat in the Third Anglo-Maratha War (1817–18).
